summary.title: Guerrilla Capacity Planning: A Tactical Approach to Planning for Highly Scalable Applications and Services
summary.one_liner: A book-based introduction to capacity planning for scalable systems, covering the universal scalability law and how to fit its coefficients to measured throughput.
keywords: how to plan capacity for scalable systems
how to fit scalability curve to throughput data
takeaways: The universal scalability law models how throughput scales with load, accounting for contention and coherency effects.
The page describes a procedure for fitting the law's coefficients to measured throughput data.
The book is a tactical, practical guide to capacity planning for highly scalable applications and services.
Topics include ITIL, virtualization, website and internet planning, and a going-guerrilla case study.
summary.summary: This is the landing page for N. J. Gunther's book Guerrilla Capacity Planning, published by Springer in 2006 (about 250 pages, ISBN 9783540261384). The page is mostly a table of contents with chapter titles, ordering and availability details, and an erratum form. From the listing, the book derives the universal scalability law and gives a procedure for fitting its coefficients to measured throughput. The chapter list covers topics such as Amdahl's law, NUMA parameters, virtualization, and website and internet planning. The page itself gives few technical details beyond these topics.
